citations.chunk_id: 0038_Liu 等 - 2024 - Ester-based anti-freezing electrolyte achieving ultra-low temperature cycling for sodium-ion batteri::sec11::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively.

association_citations.quote: In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively.

To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). association_citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2
association_citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

association_citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child3
association_citations.quote: This enhanced stability primarily arises from the formation of NaF-enriched gradient CEI/SEI layers, which effectively suppress electrolyte decomposition at elevated temperatures. In addition, the NVP||HC full cell employing the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 100 cycles under the extreme conditions of high voltage (4.3 V) and 50 °C (Figure S42, Supporting Information). The NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte exhibits remarkable temperature adaptability across a broad temperature range. At low temperatures of -20 and -40 °C, the NTM-based electrolyte still delivers high discharge capacities of 71.5 mA h g $^{-1}$ and 62.2 mA h g $^{-1}$ , corresponding to 83.2% and 72.4% of the discharge capacity at room temperature, respectively (Figure 5g). Additionally, the battery can stably complete 50 discharge cycles at -20 °C (Figure S43, Supporting Information), and even successfully operate for 20 cycles at -40 °C, maintaining a capacity retention rate of 83.9% (Figure 5h; Figure S44, Supporting Information). Benefiting from the excellent anti-freezing capability and low-temperature ionic conductivity of the NTM electrolyte, the NVP||HC full cell delivers an average specific capacity of 31.8 mA h g $^{-1}$ at -60 °C (Figure S45, Supporting Information).

At -40 °C, the NVP||Na cell with NP electrolyte delivers only 22.8 mA h g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , owing to its low ionic conductivity and sluggish ion transport. citations.quote: Fig. 5h compares the wide-temperature performance of NTP||NVP full cells with other reported sodium-ion batteries in terms of actual capacity (AC) to theoretical capacity (TC) ratio at different temperatures [44,47–50]. To further prove the fast-charging and widely operated performance of NTP||NVP sodium-ion battery system, we assembled a 1 Ah-level sodium-ion pouch cell. As shown in Fig. 6a, the pouch cell was composed of cathode (NVP), anode (NTP), separators (polypropylene-polyethylene composite), tabs (Al), electrolyte (1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in DIGYDME) and shell (aluminum-plastic composite film). The detailed parameters of NTP||NVP pouch cell was shown in Table S5. As shown in Fig. 6b, the pouch cell showed a reversible capacity of 1.2 Ah with an average working potential of 1.2 V (insert the picture of pouch cell) under room temperature. citations.quote: As depicted in Fig. 5a, the NTP||NVP full cell demonstrated the specific capacity of 108 mAh g $^{-1}$ and 105 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 and 0 °C, respectively. Even the test temperature decreased to -40 °C, the full cell still maintained a reversible capacity of 75 mAh g $^{-1}$ , approximately 64 % of the capacity than it at room temperature. This impressive performance can be attributed to the low freezing point of ether-based electrolytes, enabling normal operation and high capacity at -40 °C. Despite some polarization at low temperatures, the discharge plateau of the NTP anode remains above -40 °C, effectively preventing sodium precipitation and ensuring safe cell operation. The cycling stability and rate capacity of the NTP||NVP cell at -40 °C were also assessed. As shown in Fig. 5b, the cell exhibited a remarkable rate capacity at -40 °C, retaining 72 % capacity from 0.1 to 1 C. Fig. 5c shows the cycle stability of NTP||NVP full cell, which demonstrates an excellent 93.1 % capacity retention after 180 cycles at 0.1 C. Following the high/low-temperature performance evaluation, we examined the high-temperature stability of the NTP||NVP cell from 30 to 60 °C. The constant-current charge/discharge curves in Fig. 5d indicate discharge capacities of 104.6, 108, and 112.2 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 30, 40, and 50 °C, respectively. Even at 60 °C, the cell delivered a reversible discharge specific capacity of 112.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ with an average coulombic efficiency of more than 99 %.

To further prove the fast-charging and widely operated performance of NTP||NVP sodium-ion battery system, we assembled a 1 Ah-level sodium-ion pouch cell. As shown in Fig. 6a, the pouch cell was composed of cathode (NVP), anode (NTP), separators (polypropylene-polyethylene composite), tabs (Al), electrolyte (1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in DIGYDME) and shell (aluminum-plastic composite film). The detailed parameters of NTP||NVP pouch cell was shown in Table S5. As shown in Fig. 6b, the pouch cell showed a reversible capacity of 1.2 Ah with an average working potential of 1.2 V (insert the picture of pouch cell) under room temperature. The rate capability of this pouch was shown in Fig. 6c, which exhibited a reversible capacity of 1.21 Ah, 1.17 Ah, 1.11 Ah, 1.04 Ah, 1.01 Ah, and 0.95 Ah, at 0.1 C, 0.3 C, 1 C, 3 C, 5 C and 10 C, respectively, with a maximum power density of 405.6 W kg $^{-1}$ . The cycle stability of this pouch cell was shown in Fig. 6d, which showed a reversible capacity of 1.21 Ah with a capacity retention ratio of 97.6 % after 50th cycles at 0.1 C.

citations.quote: As depicted in Fig. 5a, the NTP||NVP full cell demonstrated the specific capacity of 108 mAh g $^{-1}$ and 105 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 and 0 °C, respectively. Even the test temperature decreased to -40 °C, the full cell still maintained a reversible capacity of 75 mAh g $^{-1}$ , approximately 64 % of the capacity than it at room temperature. This impressive performance can be attributed to the low freezing point of ether-based electrolytes, enabling normal operation and high capacity at -40 °C. Despite some polarization at low temperatures, the discharge plateau of the NTP anode remains above -40 °C, effectively preventing sodium precipitation and ensuring safe cell operation. The cycling stability and rate capacity of the NTP||NVP cell at -40 °C were also assessed. As shown in Fig. 5b, the cell exhibited a remarkable rate capacity at -40 °C, retaining 72 % capacity from 0.1 to 1 C. Fig. 5c shows the cycle stability of NTP||NVP full cell, which demonstrates an excellent 93.1 % capacity retention after 180 cycles at 0.1 C. Following the high/low-temperature performance evaluation, we examined the high-temperature stability of the NTP||NVP cell from 30 to 60 °C. The constant-current charge/discharge curves in Fig. 5d indicate discharge capacities of 104.6, 108, and 112.2 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 30, 40, and 50 °C, respectively. Even at 60 °C, the cell delivered a reversible discharge specific capacity of 112.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ with an average coulombic efficiency of more than 99 %.

2.4. Electrochemical Performance of Full Cell
We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). This indicates that temperature-adaptive electrolytes are not only compatible with NVP, but can also upgrade the rate performance and low-temperature performance of NVP cathode.

To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g $^{-1}$ in Figure 6a. After cycling 100 cycles at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 86.7%. Then, the pouch cell was cycled 100 cycles at -30 °C, and the capacity retention rate was 92.43% in Figure 6e. Therefore, 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL electrolyte with a temperature-adaptive solvent structure holds great potential in the practical application of SIBs.

citations.quote:
Yuewei Cui, Youxuan Ni, Yuankun Wang, Linyue Wang, Wenxuan Yang, Shuang Wu, Weiwei Xie, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan,\* and Jun Chen\*

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. The desolvation of $Na^{+}$ is a crucial step in impeding the transport of $Na^{+}$ , which primarily attributes to the robust solvent coordination of $Na^{+}$ . Herein, a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with an ultraweakly coordinated 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) is designed for constructing anion-rich solvation structure in a diglyme (G2)-based electrolyte. The electronegativity of the oxygen atoms of G2 is attenuated by dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2. As the temperature drops, the weakened $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) interaction leads to increased anionic coordination and less solvent coordination, facilitating the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ . This anionic-enhanced solvation structure contributes to the formation of stable solid electrolyte interface at the hard carbon (HC) anode, which accelerates $Na^{+}$ transport and diminishing the voltage polarization at low temperatures. Consequently, the HC anode can retain a high capacity of 203.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -50 °C, and the pouch cell composed of $HC||Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ at -30 °C achieves a capacity retention of 92.43% after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

association_citations.quote:
Yuewei Cui, Youxuan Ni, Yuankun Wang, Linyue Wang, Wenxuan Yang, Shuang Wu, Weiwei Xie, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan,\* and Jun Chen\*

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. The desolvation of $Na^{+}$ is a crucial step in impeding the transport of $Na^{+}$ , which primarily attributes to the robust solvent coordination of $Na^{+}$ . Herein, a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with an ultraweakly coordinated 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) is designed for constructing anion-rich solvation structure in a diglyme (G2)-based electrolyte. The electronegativity of the oxygen atoms of G2 is attenuated by dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2. As the temperature drops, the weakened $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) interaction leads to increased anionic coordination and less solvent coordination, facilitating the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ . This anionic-enhanced solvation structure contributes to the formation of stable solid electrolyte interface at the hard carbon (HC) anode, which accelerates $Na^{+}$ transport and diminishing the voltage polarization at low temperatures. Consequently, the HC anode can retain a high capacity of 203.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -50 °C, and the pouch cell composed of $HC||Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ at -30 °C achieves a capacity retention of 92.43% after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

The only residual gap is that no direct -40 °C, 100-cycle pouch-cell measurement is reported; this is a limited gap, not a contradiction, so the electrolyte is recommended for selection while noting that the -40 °C pouch combination remains to be confirmed.

citations.quote: To quantitatively elucidate the solvation structure of the two electrolytes, classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed at 25 °C. The radial distribution function (RDF) in Figure 2e,f displays the distribution of each component around $Na^{+}$ in two electrolytes at 25 °C. The average coordination number (CN) values of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) in 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 and 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL are 5.979 and 4.733, respectively. The CN of Na–F ( $PF_{6}^{-}$ ) increases from 0.233 to 1.092, as shown in Figure 2g and Table S1 (Supporting Information). This indeed indicates that DOL weakens the coordination oxygen activity of G2, thereby reducing the coordination of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) and increasing the coordination of anions. The phase transition temperatures of the two electrolytes were evaluated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and cryopolarizing microscope. Remarkably, the melting point of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL is $-91$ °C, while the melting point of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 is only $-46$ °C, as shown in Figure 2h. Moreover, 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2 generates small ice crystals at $-50$ °C and emerges a large-scale phase transition at $-70$ °C. 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL is a pure liquid at $-50$ °C and solvent crystallization does not occur until it is cooled to $-110$ °C (Figure S3, Supporting Information). Variable temperature viscosity tests were conducted on these two electrolytes in Figure 2i.

citations.quote: As the most commonly used electrolyte for SIBs, a PC-based electrolyte composed of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -PC/FEC was used as the control (hereafter referred to as PC) [42,43]. Similarly, the proposed carboxylate ester-based electrolytes in this work are composed of MP, FEC, and NaPF $_{6}$ . Firstly, the influence of concentration on electrochemical stability and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte was investigated, and as shown in Fig. S1(a), the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte with 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ is significantly higher than that of the electrolyte with 2 M NaPF $_{6}$ . Moreover, the MP-based electrolyte with 2 M NaPF $_{6}$ has better electrochemical stability (Fig. S1(b)), therefore 2 M NaPF $_{6}$ -MP/FEC was selected for research, which will be referred to as MP in the following. The redox reaction activities of isolated solvents and sodium salt of MP and PC-based electrolytes are investigated with frontier molecular orbital theory, involving the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) and highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy levels (Fig. 1(a)). The LUMO/HOMO energy level of MP is close to PC, which indicates MP has considerable oxidation/reduction stability compared to PC. In addition, the HOMO level of FEC is lower than that of the other solvents, indicating the stronger capability of the free fluorinated carbonate solvent against oxidation.

citations.quote: In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively.

citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

Particularly at extremely low temperatures, the electrolyte's antifreezing properties are critical to ensuring battery operability. $^{[44]}$ Digital photographs show that the NTM electrolyte retains good fluidity without phase transition even when the temperature drops to $-60\ ^{\circ}C$ , thereby demonstrating superior anti-freezing properties (Figure S21, Supporting Information). Figures 4a and S22 (Supporting Information) show that the NP electrolyte shows a sharp decline in ionic conductivity below $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ due to the high viscosity of PC. In contrast, the NTM electrolyte exhibits superior ionic conductivity across the entire temperature range, particularly at sub-zero conditions, and exhibits lower activation energies for ion transport from $50\ ^{\circ}C$ to $-50\ ^{\circ}C$ (1.24 and 2.00 kJ mol $^{-1}$ vs. 2.00 and 3.04 kJ mol $^{-1}$ for NT vs. 2.32 and 4.91 kJ mol $^{-1}$ for NP). citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

association_citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2
association_citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: Fig. 5h compares the wide-temperature performance of NTP||NVP full cells with other reported sodium-ion batteries in terms of actual capacity (AC) to theoretical capacity (TC) ratio at different temperatures [44,47–50]. To further prove the fast-charging and widely operated performance of NTP||NVP sodium-ion battery system, we assembled a 1 Ah-level sodium-ion pouch cell. As shown in Fig. 6a, the pouch cell was composed of cathode (NVP), anode (NTP), separators (polypropylene-polyethylene composite), tabs (Al), electrolyte (1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in DIGYDME) and shell (aluminum-plastic composite film). The detailed parameters of NTP||NVP pouch cell was shown in Table S5. As shown in Fig. 6b, the pouch cell showed a reversible capacity of 1.2 Ah with an average working potential of 1.2 V (insert the picture of pouch cell) under room temperature. The rate capability of this pouch was shown in Fig. 6c, which exhibited a reversible capacity of 1.21 Ah, 1.17 Ah, 1.11 Ah, 1.04 Ah, 1.01 Ah, and 0.95 Ah, at 0.1 C, 0.3 C, 1 C, 3 C, 5 C and 10 C, respectively, with a maximum power density of 405.6 W kg $^{-1}$ . The cycle stability of this pouch cell was shown in Fig. 6d, which showed a reversible capacity of 1.21 Ah with a capacity retention ratio of 97.6 % after 50th cycles at 0.1 C.

citations.quote: As depicted in Fig. 5a, the NTP||NVP full cell demonstrated the specific capacity of 108 mAh g $^{-1}$ and 105 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 and 0 °C, respectively. Even the test temperature decreased to -40 °C, the full cell still maintained a reversible capacity of 75 mAh g $^{-1}$ , approximately 64 % of the capacity than it at room temperature. This impressive performance can be attributed to the low freezing point of ether-based electrolytes, enabling normal operation and high capacity at -40 °C. Despite some polarization at low temperatures, the discharge plateau of the NTP anode remains above -40 °C, effectively preventing sodium precipitation and ensuring safe cell operation. The cycling stability and rate capacity of the NTP||NVP cell at -40 °C were also assessed. As shown in Fig. 5b, the cell exhibited a remarkable rate capacity at -40 °C, retaining 72 % capacity from 0.1 to 1 C. Fig. 5c shows the cycle stability of NTP||NVP full cell, which demonstrates an excellent 93.1 % capacity retention after 180 cycles at 0.1 C. Following the high/low-temperature performance evaluation, we examined the high-temperature stability of the NTP||NVP cell from 30 to 60 °C. The constant-current charge/discharge curves in Fig. 5d indicate discharge capacities of 104.6, 108, and 112.2 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 30, 40, and 50 °C, respectively. Even at 60 °C, the cell delivered a reversible discharge specific capacity of 112.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ with an average coulombic efficiency of more than 99 %.

## 配方筛选结果
已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。

### 候选资料：cand-1-napf6-g2dol（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：G2 (diglyme), DOL (1,3-dioxolane)；溶剂比例（体积）：G2=1.0, DOL=3.0。
- 配方原文 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]：Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

### 候选资料：cand-2-napf6-g2-reference（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：G2 (diglyme)；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：G2=1.0。
- 配方原文 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]：Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

### 候选资料：cand-3-napf6-mp-fec（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：methyl propionate (MP), FEC；溶剂比例（体积）：MP=9.0, FEC=1.0。
- 配方原文 [0038_Liu 等 - 2024 - Ester-based anti-freezing electrolyte achieving ultra-low temperature cycling for sodium-ion batteri::sec6::child0]：The electrolyte is prepared in an argon-filled glove box, where the water and oxygen contents are both less than 0.1 ppm. The electrolyte we designed for this work is 2 M NaPF $_{6}$ (DoDoChem, >99.8%) dissolved in methyl propionate (MP, >99%, Macklin) and FEC (DoDoChem, >99.9%) at 9:1 (vol.%). The control electrolyte is 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ dissolved in PC (Sigma Aldrich, >99%) and FEC at 9:1 (vol.%).

### 候选资料：cand-4-napf6-tep-mp-vc（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：TEP, MP；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=6.0, MP=4.0；添加剂：VC；添加剂用量：VC=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2]：The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

### 候选资料：cand-5-napf6-digdme（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：DIG (diglyme), DME。
- 配方原文 [0370_Zhang 等 - 2025 - All climate and fast-charging sodium-ion pouch cell::sec7::child19]：Fig. 5h compares the wide-temperature performance of NTP||NVP full cells with other reported sodium-ion batteries in terms of actual capacity (AC) to theoretical capacity (TC) ratio at different temperatures [44,47–50]. To further prove the fast-charging and widely operated performance of NTP||NVP sodium-ion battery system, we assembled a 1 Ah-level sodium-ion pouch cell. As shown in Fig. 6a, the pouch cell was composed of cathode (NVP), anode (NTP), separators (polypropylene-polyethylene composite), tabs (Al), electrolyte (1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in DIGYDME) and shell (aluminum-plastic composite film). The detailed parameters of NTP||NVP pouch cell was shown in Table S5. As shown in Fig. 6b, the pouch cell showed a reversible capacity of 1.2 Ah with an average working potential of 1.2 V (insert the picture of pouch cell) under room temperature. The rate capability of this pouch was shown in Fig. 6c, which exhibited a reversible capacity of 1.21 Ah, 1.17 Ah, 1.11 Ah, 1.04 Ah, 1.01 Ah, and 0.95 Ah, at 0.1 C, 0.3 C, 1 C, 3 C, 5 C and 10 C, respectively, with a maximum power density of 405.6 W kg $^{-1}$ . The cycle stability of this pouch cell was shown in Fig. 6d, which showed a reversible capacity of 1.21 Ah with a capacity retention ratio of 97.6 % after 50th cycles at 0.1 C.

## 候选评估
### cand-1-napf6-g2dol
评估建议：The candidate is the paper's own electrolyte for exactly this HC||NVP cold-resistant SIB target: 0.5 M NaPF6 in 3:1 vol DOL:G2 is directly demonstrated with a 45 mAh HC||NVP pouch cell (100 cycles, 92.43% retention at -30 °C) and with -40 °C full-cell cycling (92.8% over 100 cumulative cycles), giving strong format- and temperature-adjacent support. The only residual gap is that no direct -40 °C, 100-cycle pouch-cell measurement is reported; this is a limited gap, not a contradiction, so the electrolyte is recommended for selection while noting that the -40 °C pouch combination remains to be confirmed.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Electrolyte salt and concentration: 0.5 M NaPF6：The source states the electrolyte is 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL and uses 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 as reference, matching the candidate salt and concentration. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]
- Solvent system G2/DOL with DOL:G2 volume ratio of 3:1：The text says DOL was blended into 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1, and Figure 2 uses G2/DOL (1:3, vol.), matching the candidate's G2=1.0/DOL=3.0 volume basis. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child2]
- Cell chemistry: hard carbon (HC) anode paired with NVP (Na3V2(PO4)3) cathode：The paper reports Na3V2(PO4)3 cathode coin cells and a HC||NVP full cell, and an HC||Na3V2(PO4)3 pouch cell, matching the target chemistry. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec0::child0]
- Cell format: 45 mAh pouch cell：The source explicitly states a piece pouch cell (45 mAh) was assembled for cycling testing, matching the requested 45 mAh pouch format. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1]
- Cycling duration of 100 cycles：The pouch cell was cycled 100 cycles at 25 °C and then 100 cycles at -30 °C, and the abstract states 100 cycles, matching the 100-cycle requirement. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec0::child0]
- Target observable: cycle-capacity retention：The paper reports capacity retention rates (86.7% after 100 cycles at 25 °C; 92.43% after 100 cycles at -30 °C; 92.8% for the -40 °C full-cell segment), which is exactly the requested observable. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1]
- Operation at -40 °C：For this electrolyte the full cell preserved 64.8% capacity at -40 °C and, over 50 cycles at 25 °C plus 50 cycles at -40 °C, retained 92.8%; the HC anode operational range supports -40 °C capability, so -40 °C performance is directly demonstrated (in coin full cell). [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec0::child0]
- The 45 mAh HC||NVP pouch cell itself operated at -40 °C：The 45 mAh pouch cell was cycled at 25 °C and then -30 °C (92.43% over 100 cycles), while the -40 °C cycling data come from a coin full cell; no source statement transfers the pouch-cell result to -40 °C, so this exact combination is not directly reported. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5]
文献与候选的关联：The same formulation (0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL, DOL:G2 = 3:1 vol) is the electrolyte used across the Na||NVP coin cell, the HC||NVP coin full cell, and the 45 mAh HC||NVP pouch cell; the chemistry/format/observable chain is thus linked by a single, explicitly named electrolyte, though the -40 °C cycling is on coin full cells and the 45 mAh pouch cell is only cycled at -30 °C. [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1][0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec0::child0]
